# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 61 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | Coptic

---

## Saying 61

Jesus said: "Two will rest on a bed; one will die, one will live." Salome said: "Who are you, man? You have reclined on my couch as one from the same and eaten from my table." Jesus said to her: "I am the one who comes from what is whole. I was given from the things of my Father." Salome said: "I am your disciple." Jesus said: "Therefore I say: when someone is whole, he will be filled with light; but when he is divided, he will be filled with darkness."

---

**Council Notes:**

- "Man" (EMET) rather than "sir" (LOGOS): the Coptic *rōme* is the word for "man/person," not a title of respect. Salome's address may carry a note of surprise or challenge.
- "What is whole" (*petjek*): EMET and SOPHIA preserve the nominal form; PNEUMA's "undivided" is theologically interesting but substitutes a negative for a positive concept.
- The fragmented dialogue: scholarly consensus attributes "I am your disciple" to Salome. Brackets or attribution both acceptable; SOPHIA uses attribution without brackets for readability.
- The conclusion (whole → light / divided → darkness) is the interpretive key: wholeness (*teleios*) as the Thomasine ideal, versus division as spiritual death.
- The Q-parallel opening (Luke 17:34) is preserved but serves as a frame for the unique Salome dialogue.
